    not ask to lose. The destination is the surface the editing was reached from rather than the case's own detail
    view, because this specification has already decided this same gesture — leaving an authoring surface without
    submitting — three times, and all three land on the surface the authoring was reached from (an-abandoned-revision-composition-writes-nothing,
    an-abandoned-capability-registration-entry-registers-nothing and a-connector-configuration-authoring-may-be-abandoned-without-registering),
    and this log's own entry for the second of those records an earlier fixed-destination value being replaced for
    precisely this reason, that one gesture answering two ways is one specification giving two answers. A fixed
    case-detail destination is also wrong on the readings that matter, since a curator who reached the editing from
    a listing of the case's versions or from that version's own manifest would be moved somewhere they never came
    from. Nothing is lost by the reached-from reading, because a-listed-case-version-offers-a-route-to-its-own-manifest
    owes its route on every reading of the listing regardless. Home is a new rule rather than an extension of an-abandoned-revision-composition-writes-nothing,
    because that rule is written over composing a revision of a hypothesis while this is the distinct act over the
    version's own attributes and manifest, the same separation the integration context already keeps between its
    two abandonment rules. An invariant rather than a policy, immediate, because case-version is the aggregate root
    and manifest-entry is the value object it composes, the same pairing a-case-version-is-written-once already
    constrains as one invariant.
- location: rules/integration/a-successful-connector-registration-lands-on-the-configurations-own-surface.md
  field: statement
  unstated: No node states where an operator who submitted a connector configuration registration is taken once
    that registration succeeds. contracts/integration/connector-configuration-registry publishes register-connector
    alongside read-connector-configuration and list-connector-configurations; a-connector-configuration-authoring-may-be-abandoned-without-registering
    decides the destination for an authoring left without registering, a-connector-configuration-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-listing
    decides that a route to the listing is owed from the surface, and a-submitted-registration-states-its-outcome-to-the-operator
    states what the operator is told about the outcome while expressly leaving where the surface then goes undecided
    — so whether the operator lands at the configuration's own connector name, at the listing, or stays on the authoring
    surface fell to whatever an interface happened to render.
  decided: The surface addressed by that configuration's own connector name — the one read-connector-configuration
    answers — in both branches of register-connector's create-or-replace; not the listing of registered connector
    configurations, and not the authoring surface the registration was submitted from. Recorded as a new invariant
    over domain/integration/connector-configuration.
  why: A successful submission leaves a configuration standing under the connector name the registration carried,
    so the destination keyed on that name answers — the exact hazard a-connector-configuration-authoring-may-be-abandoned-without-registering
    takes the reached-from surface to avoid (a-connector-configuration-read-by-an-unregistered-name-is-refused refusing
    a name nothing has registered) is what a success removes, which is why abandonment and success land differently
    without answering one question two ways, the two acts leaving different things standing. The sibling registry's
    own landing was decided this same way in a-successful-capability-registration-lands-on-the-capabilitys-own-surface,
    and the one difference between the two — that this registry states its unregistered-name refusal in a rule of
    its own while the capability registry states its own in constraints/the-capability-identity-read-refuses-an-unregistered-identity
    — bears on where each refusal is recorded and what it tells a caller, never on whether the identity-keyed read
    answers once a registration stands, which is the only thing this destination turns on; deciding it the other
    way here would repeat the correction this log already records against an-abandoned-capability-registration-entry-registers-nothing,
    where one gesture answered two ways across the two registries was replaced for exactly that reason. Staying
    on the authoring surface makes a submission that succeeded indistinguishable from one not yet made, and worse,
    domain/integration/connector-configuration is replaced whole on every edit, so the act that surface still offers
    is a second register-connector under the same name, now a total replacement of what was just registered. The
    listing is refused because constraints/listings-are-paged answers list-connector-configurations one page at
    a time and which page the new registration falls on is that constraint's answer, so the operator would land
    where their own registration is not reliably in view; nothing is lost by it, since a-connector-configuration-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-listing
    owes a route to that listing on every reading of the surface this lands on. Home is a new rule rather than the
    api contract, which cannot declare a presentation, and rather than the domain element, which declares what a
    configuration is and not what a surface does with one. An invariant, immediate, because both facts it rests
    on are that one element's own.
- location: rules/integration/a-loaded-registration-edit-may-be-discarded-without-leaving-the-surface.md
  field: statement
  unstated: No node states whether an operator who has edited a capability registration or a connector configuration
    on the surface that read it may put the unsubmitted edit down and take the read content back without leaving
    that surface, nor whether such an act takes a further act from the operator before it happens. The two registries'
    contracts publish one write and their reads and say nothing about an edit never submitted; every registration
    rule in the integration context is written over what a submission carries; the four abandonment rules of this
    specification all state a leaving, writing nothing and returning the operator to the surface the authoring was
    reached from, and none of them states an act in which the operator stays; and both route rules explicitly leave
    open what becomes of content an authoring surface holds unwritten. So neither the availability of a discard
    in place, the content it would restore, the surfaces it is offered on, nor whether it is confirmed was decided.
  decided: An operator editing, on the surface that read it, the capability registered at a name and version or
    the connector configuration registered under a connector name is offered an act returning every field of that
    surface to the content of the registration the surface last read, registering nothing and leaving the operator
    on that same surface; the act takes effect only where the operator states in a further, explicit act that it
    is to be performed, and otherwise the edit stands untouched. A surface holding no read registration — one authoring
    at an identity nothing is registered at, one whose read has not answered, one whose read failed — is offered
    no such act. Recorded as a new policy over domain/integration/capability and domain/integration/connector-configuration,
    eventual.
  why: 'Offered, because the way out this specification already states is a leaving and not a putting-down: the
    four abandonment rules each end the operator''s work at the surface and land them on the surface the authoring
    was reached from, so an operator who wants the read content back and wants to go on editing has only leave-and-return,
    and returning directly is not owed — a-single-capability-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-capabilities-listing
    and a-connector-configuration-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-listing owe a route to the listing, so the return
    runs through the set to arrive at content the surface was already holding. What is recovered cannot be retyped,
    a connector configuration being opaque text and a capability''s contract carrying both schemas. Restricted to
    surfaces that read a registration, because a surface authoring at an unregistered identity read nothing to go
    back to, emptying its fields recovering nothing and being indistinguishable from the operator clearing them,
    while a-capability-keyed-surface-states-a-read-in-flight-and-a-read-that-failed and a-presented-connector-configuration-states-an-outstanding-or-failed-read
    already hold that no registration content is presented in the outstanding and failed windows. Confirmed, because
    the discard destroys content held nowhere else and no operation of either contract can answer it back, and because
    it differs from the abandonment in the one respect that bears on protection: an abandonment ends the operator''s
    engagement and shows itself by landing them elsewhere, while a discard leaves them on the same surface and continuing,
    so a mis-triggered one is built upon — the next edit is made over content silently reverted, and may be submitted
    over a write both registries make total. A second operator act is the least that separates the discard asked
    for from the discard mis-triggered, and this specification already reads a costly act as the operator''s own
    to state rather than a surface''s to infer. One rule for both registries, on a-submitted-registration-states-its-outcome-to-the-operator''s
    own reasoning that the two are the same shape in every particular that bears on this. A policy at eventual consistency,
    matching that sibling, because the content restored is what a read issued separately to a registry answered
    and the surface never holds it. Disclosed here, as this route requires: the material for this decision included
    a survey of the delivered frontend, which reports that the two detail surfaces already offer a confirmed discard
    control and the two create surfaces do not, so this decision was taken over material derived from source already
    written and may be the specification agreeing with what was already built rather than deciding independently
    of it; the reasoning above rests on the specification''s own standing rules, and a reviewer who rejects it rejects
    that reasoning.'
- location: rules/knowledge/releasing-or-discarding-a-draft-case-version-takes-a-further-explicit-act.md
  field: statement
  unstated: Whether releasing a draft case version, and whether discarding one, each require the curator to state
    in a further explicit act — after choosing the act and before it happens — that it is to be performed; whether
    either may be performed other than through that further act; and, for the discard, whether that further act
    requires the curator to reproduce the case's own slug. contracts/knowledge/case-lifecycle publishes both acts
    and a-case-version-moves-through-its-declared-lifecycle, only-a-draft-case-version-may-be-discarded and a-case-version-is-written-once
    state when each is refused and what each leaves behind, but no node states how the curator's own act reaches
    them; a-surface-offering-release-states-which-release-conditions-the-draft-meets states only what a surface
    discloses before a release is attempted and expressly says nothing about whether the release may then be attempted.
  decided: 'Both acts take a further explicit act and neither is performed on the asking alone: a release and a
    discard of a draft case version each take effect only where the curator, having asked for that act, states in
    a further act that it is to be performed, and where the curator does not so state the version stands in draft
    exactly as it stood. The two further acts are not identical: the discard''s is performed only where the curator
    reproduces the case''s own slug in it, and an act reproducing no slug or a slug that is not the case''s issues
    no discard; the release''s carries the statement alone.'
  why: 'The further act is owed for both because this specification already reads an act it cannot answer back as
    one the curator states rather than one a surface infers — a-loaded-registration-edit-may-be-discarded-without-leaving-the-surface,
    on the ground that the act destroys content nothing published can restore and, unlike an abandonment, leaves
    the actor where they were and continuing. Both acts here meet that ground more squarely, since what they freeze
    or destroy is the stored version rather than an edit the surface held: released is terminal and never altered
    again (a-case-version-moves-through-its-declared-lifecycle, a-case-version-is-written-once), a discard removes
    the version and its manifest entries and spends its number (only-a-draft-case-version-may-be-discarded, a-case-version-number-is-never-reused),
    and contracts/knowledge/case-lifecycle publishes nothing that undoes either. The slug is required of the discard
    and not of the release because the two do not destroy the same kind of thing: a release ends a draft by making
    it answer for investigations forever and everything it produced remains readable, while a discard ends a draft
    by removing it, taking its manifest entries and spending its number, so what the curator composed is gone rather
    than frozen and no reading recovers it; reproducing the slug is what makes the destroying act one no curator
    completes without naming what is being destroyed. That a case holds at most one draft (a-case-has-at-most-one-draft)
    settles which version a discard would take and settles nothing about whether the curator meant to take it —
    the slug answers intent, not ambiguity. Disclosure of a rejected reading, as this log exists to carry: the blind
    judge that decided this fact decided the further act for both acts in the same shape and expressly refused the
    slug, on the grounds that no act this specification states asks anyone to retype an identity, that a-case-has-at-most-one-draft
    closes the wrong-draft hazard, and that requiring the slug for the discard alone protects the removal of a draft
    nothing ever pinned more heavily than the release nothing may undo. The human running this planning rejected
    that half of the reading and stated the value recorded here, on the ground that the discard destroys where the
    release preserves; the judge''s reasoning is recorded here rather than discarded so a later reviewer can weigh
    both and reopen it. The material for this fact also included a survey of the delivered frontend, which reports
    both acts already confirmed there and the discard''s confirmation already demanding the typed slug, so this
    entry agrees with what stands built and a reviewer should read it knowing that.'
- location: rules/knowledge/a-newly-created-draft-offers-no-act-before-its-own-record-arrives.md
  field: statement
  unstated: Whether a surface presenting a newly created draft case version offers the acts over that version —
    its release, its discard, and the correction of its own declared attributes — while no answer for that version's
    own record has arrived, or offers none of them until that record has been read. a-draft-versions-content-is-presented-only-from-its-own-record
    decides only what content that surface states in that interval and closes by saying it decides the source of
    the content and what is said while none has arrived, nothing more; contracts/knowledge/case-lifecycle publishes
    release, discard and update-draft without stating when a surface offers them; a-surface-offering-release-states-which-release-conditions-the-draft-meets
    expressly leaves whether the release offer is made at all to other nodes; and no rule, scenario or constraint
    in the knowledge context states what any surface offers while a read it stands on has not answered.
  decided: 'None of the three acts is offered while no answer for that version''s own record has arrived: the surface
    offers no act whose performance issues a release, a discard or an update-draft over that version. The withholding
    lasts exactly that interval, turns on nothing else — not on the values the creating request carried, not on
    the version the manifest was copied from, not on the surface the creation was reached from — and touches neither
    the leaving an-abandoned-case-version-edit-writes-nothing states nor any route the specification owes. Recorded
    as a new invariant over domain/knowledge/case-version, matching the type and constrains of its sibling a-draft-versions-content-is-presented-only-from-its-own-record.'
  why: 'Each of the three acts is performed against content the specification has already forbidden this surface
    to show in this interval, so offering them offers acts over a record nobody has read. For the correction, a-presented-case-version-states-its-own-declared-attributes
    has already written down the harm in this exact pairing — a correction made against values the curator cannot
    see is made blind and overwrites what nobody read — and in this interval, by the sibling rule''s own decision,
    no attribute of the version is stated at all. For release and discard, both endings are irreversible in their
    own direction, and what would be ended is content the curator never composed — a-new-drafts-manifest-is-copied-from-an-existing-version
    makes the draft''s starting manifest the case''s own existing version''s — and has not yet read; additionally,
    the only disclosure a release-offering surface owes is empty here, since a-surface-offering-release-states-which-release-conditions-the-draft-meets
    would have every condition it names stated as not yet decided. The withholding is also the answer this specification
    has already given twice for the same question in the integration context: a-loaded-registration-edit-may-be-discarded-without-leaving-the-surface
    offers its act on no surface whose read has not answered, and a-capability-keyed-surface-states-a-read-in-flight-and-a-read-that-failed
    stands its one control in the failed window and in neither of the other two, so deciding it the other way here
    would give one specification two answers. Nothing is lost by waiting: the interval ends with an answer the surface
    is already awaiting, the leaving that writes nothing stays available, and no call is refused by this rule. Disclosed
    as this route requires: the material included a survey of the delivered frontend reporting that the new-draft
    screen already withholds its action row while that read is outstanding, so this decision was taken over material
    derived from source already written and may be the specification agreeing with what was built rather than deciding
    independently of it.'
- location: rules/integration/an-abandonment-with-no-surface-to-return-to-lands-on-the-registrys-listing.md
  field: statement
  unstated: No node states where an operator is landed when they leave, without registering, an authoring surface
    of either integration registry that was reached from no surface — its address opened directly or reloaded, so
    that the surface the authoring was reached from does not exist. an-abandoned-capability-registration-entry-registers-nothing
    and a-connector-configuration-authoring-may-be-abandoned-without-registering both state the destination only
    as that reached-from surface, and both registries publish identity-keyed reads made for surfaces that load on
    first navigation or a page refresh (read-capability-by-identity, read-connector-configuration), so the reading
    is an ordinary one whose destination the two rules name nothing for; the two route rules owe a route to each
    listing but state no landing for a leaving, so where the operator ends up fell to whatever an interface happened
    to do.
  decided: The listing of the registry the authoring surface authors into — the listing list-capabilities of contracts/integration/capability-registry
    answers for a capability authoring surface, and the listing list-connector-configurations of contracts/integration/connector-configuration-registry
    answers for a connector configuration authoring surface — with nothing registered and every registration left
    as it stood, and with neither the authoring surface itself nor a read keyed on the identity being authored as
    the destination. Recorded as a new policy over domain/integration/capability and domain/integration/connector-configuration,
    eventual, stating only the case where no reached-from surface exists and leaving the two abandonment rules'
    destination untouched wherever one does.
  why: 'The destination must answer, which is the property the two abandonment rules chose the reached-from surface
    for ("having answered once already"): the two listings answer from what is currently registered and, under constraints/listings-are-paged,
    answer a page with a total of zero rather than refusing, while a destination keyed on the identity being authored
    is refused by constraints/the-capability-identity-read-refuses-an-unregistered-identity and a-connector-configuration-read-by-an-unregistered-name-is-refused
    for exactly the identity an abandoned creation leaves behind. It does not reopen the return-to-the-listing reading
    the log records as replaced: that reading was rejected for privileging the listing over the surface the operator
    came from, and here there is no such surface, so the reason that rejected it does not apply and one gesture
    keeps one answer. Staying on the authoring surface is refused because a-connector-configuration-authoring-may-be-abandoned-without-registering
    states no operator is left on a surface whose only other exit is a registration they have decided against, and
    because staying is already a distinct act with its own rule, a-loaded-registration-edit-may-be-discarded-without-leaving-the-surface,
    which owes a further explicit act the abandonment does not — sharing a destination would collapse two acts the
    specification tells apart. Nothing is lost by the listing, since a-single-capability-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-capabilities-listing
    and a-connector-configuration-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-listing already owe a route to it from every reading
    of these surfaces, and the paging objection the two successful-registration rules raise against the listing
    does not reach an abandonment, which leaves no registration that has to be in view. One rule for both registries
    follows a-submitted-registration-states-its-outcome-to-the-operator and the discard rule, which already decided
    over this same pair, and answers the correction the log records against one gesture answered two ways across
    the two registries; the home is a new rule rather than either api contract, which cannot declare a presentation,
    or either domain element, which declares what a capability and a configuration are and not what a surface does
    with one.'
- location: rules/integration/an-output-schema-entry-states-what-the-system-reads-from-it.md
  field: statement
  unstated: 'Whether an operator entering a capability''s output schema is told, at the point of that entry, what
    to enter there, and what such a statement says. No node speaks to the authoring surface''s own guidance: domain/investigation/field-semantics
    states what is read out of that schema and rules/glossary/a-description-states-meaning-never-policy states what
    a description may say, both addressed to whoever reads the schema rather than to whoever types it, while a-capability-declares-its-contract,
    a-capability-declares-well-formed-schemas and a-capability-input-schema-holds-a-well-formed-object leave the
    output schema''s own shape checked at no write. The intake material fixes only that guidance stays on the screen
    and must stop reproducing those two nodes'' text and worked example; it states nothing about what the guidance
    says.'
  decided: 'A surface offering an operator entry of the output schema a capability registration declares states,
    at that entry, what the system reads out of what is entered there: that it is entered as JSON; that the fields
    it declares are the keys of that schema''s own top-level properties object; that each such key''s own type and
    description, where the schema states them, are read as that field''s declared semantics; that no other content
    of the schema is read or validated; and that a description entered there states what a value means and names
    no decision. Every claim that statement makes is one domain/investigation/field-semantics or rules/glossary/a-description-states-meaning-never-policy
    already holds — the surface states no further fact about how the schema is read, carries no worked example of
    its own, and refuses nothing on any of these grounds. Held as a new policy over domain/integration/capability
    and domain/investigation/field-semantics.'
  why: 'Told rather than not, because the output schema is the one registration attribute whose content is authored
    freely and read structurally, and no other part of the system tells the operator which part of it is load-bearing:
    a-capability-declares-well-formed-schemas checks only that the text parses, a-capability-input-schema-holds-a-well-formed-object
    records that the output schema''s properties convention is an inference never checked at registration, and field-semantics
    itself calls the rest of the schema an unenforced hint — so a schema that declares its fields anywhere else
    is accepted whole and reads downstream as no fields at all, silently costing every later citation (a-cited-field-exists-in-the-capability-output-schema)
    the vocabulary it is held to. Stating it follows this specification''s own repeated reading that an operator
    is not left an unexplained absence at a surface (a-composed-subject-presents-every-case-input-requirement''s
    explicit emptiness, a-submitted-registration-states-its-outcome-to-the-operator). The substance is bounded to
    the two nodes that already hold it, with the meaning-versus-decision half included because a description is
    published vocabulary and the entry is the one point where saying so prevents the second home that a-description-states-meaning-never-policy
    otherwise only reports; the prohibition on a further claim and on a worked example of its own is what keeps
    the screen guidance rather than a second home, which is the defect the material''s own correction names. Home
    is a new rule in rules/integration, beside every other rule governing what these authoring surfaces state, because
    domain/investigation/field-semantics is a value-object whose schema admits only attributes and an operative
    claim about what a surface states has no addressable home in it, and because a-description-states-meaning-never-policy
    governs what a description says, not what a screen says, so widening it would move a standing decision. Nothing
    is added to any element: the standing decision at domain/knowledge/case-input-requirement keeps a property''s
    own declared type and description outside what any element carries, and this decides only what the surface tells
    the person entering, carrying no schema content anywhere.'
- location: rules/integration/a-single-registration-surface-offers-a-return-to-its-origin-on-every-reading.md
  field: statement
  unstated: No node states whether a surface presenting the one capability registered at a name and version, or
    the one connector configuration registered under a connector name, offers the operator an act that registers
    nothing and lands them on the surface it was reached from on readings that hold no entry to abandon — while
    the identity-keyed or name-keyed read has not answered, where that read failed, and where that read answered
    that nothing is registered at that identity or under that name. The four abandonment rules are each written
    over an operator authoring or editing an entry not yet submitted; a-capability-keyed-surface-states-a-read-in-flight-and-a-read-that-failed
    and a-presented-connector-configuration-states-an-outstanding-or-failed-read state what those readings tell
    the operator and offer only the reattempt, in the failed window alone; a-loaded-registration-edit-may-be-discarded-without-leaving-the-surface
    expressly offers its act on none of those readings; and the two route rules owe a route to the listing, a different
    destination. So whether an operator on a reading that shows them no registration can get back to where they
    came from, and on which readings, fell to whatever an interface happened to render.
  decided: 'The act is owed on every reading, for both registries alike: a surface presenting the one capability
    registered at a name and version, or the one connector configuration registered under a connector name, offers
    the operator an act that issues no register-capability and no register-connector call and lands them on the
    surface it was reached from, present on the reading whose read has not answered, the reading whose read failed,
    the reading whose read answered that nothing is registered at that name and version or under that connector
    name, and the reading presenting the registration that read answered; its presence turns on nothing further
    — not the read''s state, not whether the operator changed anything, not which surface they came from. Where
    the operator holds an entry not yet submitted it is the act the two abandonment rules already state, with their
    destination, and not a second act. Recorded as a new policy over domain/integration/capability and domain/integration/connector-configuration,
    eventual. Not decided here: which control carries it, its wording and placement, and what becomes of content
    an authoring surface holds unwritten when it is taken.'
  why: 'Offered rather than confined to the editable reading, because this specification has already divided this
    exact interval and left this exact act inside it: a-newly-created-draft-offers-no-act-before-its-own-record-arrives
    withholds every act that writes while a surface''s read has not answered and states in the same breath that
    the withholding touches neither the leaving that writes nothing nor any route the specification owes, its reason
    being that nothing is lost by waiting precisely because the operator may still go — so deciding the other way
    here would give one specification two answers about what an unsettled read costs the operator. The unconditionality
    is the two route rules'' own reasoning over these same surfaces and these same readings: a-connector-configuration-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-listing
    holds a route present on only some readings to be one the operator cannot rely on, and names the outstanding
    and refused reads as exactly the readings where the operator has nothing on the surface to act on, and a-single-capability-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-capabilities-listing
    carries the same clause. The one restriction already placed on these readings does not transfer: a-loaded-registration-edit-may-be-discarded-without-leaving-the-surface
    excludes them because its act restores content a read answered and those readings hold none, while this act
    restores nothing and needs none; and its further explicit act is not owed either, on its own distinction that
    an act landing the operator elsewhere shows itself while one leaving them in place can be built upon unnoticed.
    The unregistered-identity reading is included because it is the one reading whose own address will never answer,
    and because an-abandoned-capability-registration-entry-registers-nothing already refuses that identity as a
    destination for that hazard while calling the reached-from surface free of it — the reasoning that rules out
    landing there rules in leaving there. Registers nothing follows from register-capability and register-connector
    being the sole writes and both being total, so leaving must stay distinguishable from registering. The destination
    is the surface it was reached from because that is what the two abandonment rules fix for this gesture, one
    of them corrected toward it in this log for the reason that one gesture answering two ways across two registries
    is one specification giving two answers. One rule for both registries on a-submitted-registration-states-its-outcome-to-the-operator''s
    own reasoning about this pair; home a new rule rather than either api contract, which cannot declare a presentation,
    or either domain element, which states what a capability and a configuration are and not what a surface offers
    over one; policy at eventual consistency because it is stated across the windows of a read the surface never
    holds, matching both siblings over this pair, and because a policy binding these two elements crosses an aggregate
    boundary. Disclosed as this route requires: the scope material describes the delivered frontend''s current controls
    — it reports that the detail surfaces'' loading and error phases today carry only a single combined control
    — so the material was partly derived from source already written; this decision departs from what is built on
    those readings rather than agreeing with it, and the material distinguishes the return-to-origin from the listing
    route without stating on which readings the former is present.'
- location: rules/integration/a-single-registration-surface-offers-a-return-to-its-origin-on-every-reading.md
  field: statement
  unstated: No node states what an operator is landed on when they take, on a surface presenting the one capability
    registered at a name and version or the one connector configuration registered under a connector name, the act
    whose whole effect is to land them on the surface it was reached from, where no such surface exists — the address
    opened directly or reloaded — and the surface holds no entry the operator has composed and not submitted. a-single-registration-surface-offers-a-return-to-its-origin-on-every-reading
    fixes that act's destination only as the surface it was reached from, which on that reading names nothing; an-abandonment-with-no-surface-to-return-to-lands-on-the-registrys-listing
    states its statement and its expression over an authoring surface and an operator who leaves it without submitting,
    so on a reading holding no composed-and-unsubmitted entry its predicate binds nothing and it reaches no destination;
    the four abandonment rules are all written over an entry not yet submitted; a-loaded-registration-edit-may-be-discarded-without-leaving-the-surface
    is expressly offered on none of the unsettled readings and keeps the operator in place besides; and the two
    route rules owe a route to the listing, which is a different act with a different obligation. So where the operator
    ends up on that reading fell to whatever an interface happened to do, including doing nothing and leaving them
    where the act exists to take them out of.
  decided: The listing of the registry whose registration the surface presents — the listing list-capabilities of
    contracts/integration/capability-registry answers where the surface presents the capability at a name and version,
    and the listing list-connector-configurations of contracts/integration/connector-configuration-registry answers
    where it presents the configuration under a connector name — on each of the four readings this rule is stated
    over alike, with nothing registered and every registration left as it stood, naming no page of the listing,
    and with neither the surface itself nor a read keyed on the name and version or the connector name it presents
    as the destination. Stated in the statement and the expression of the existing policy over domain/integration/capability
    and domain/integration/connector-configuration, bounded to the case where no reached-from surface exists and
    the surface holds no entry composed and not submitted; where such a surface exists the rule's standing destination
    is untouched, and where an entry is held this states nothing.
  why: 'The destination must answer, which is the property the abandonment rules chose the reached-from surface
    for (having answered once already): list-capabilities and list-connector-configurations answer from what is
    currently registered and, under constraints/listings-are-paged, answer a page with a total of zero rather than
    refusing, while a destination keyed on the name and version or the connector name the surface presents is refused
    by constraints/the-capability-identity-read-refuses-an-unregistered-identity and by a-connector-configuration-read-by-an-unregistered-name-is-refused
    on one of the very readings this rule covers — the read that answered that nothing is registered there — the
    same hazard an-abandoned-capability-registration-entry-registers-nothing refuses that identity for. Leaving
    the operator on the surface is refused because a-connector-configuration-authoring-may-be-abandoned-without-registering
    states that no operator is left on a surface whose only other exit is a registration they have decided against,
    because staying is already a distinct act with its own rule and its own further explicit act (a-loaded-registration-edit-may-be-discarded-without-leaving-the-surface),
    and because an act whose whole effect is to land the operator somewhere would otherwise have no effect at all
    on exactly these readings. It is the value this specification has already given to the same question — where
    does this gesture land when there is no origin — in an-abandonment-with-no-surface-to-return-to-lands-on-the-registrys-listing,
    so one question keeps one answer, and it does not reopen the return-to-the-listing reading the log records as
    replaced: that reading was rejected for privileging the listing over the surface the operator came from, and
    here there is no such surface, so the reason that rejected it has no purchase. Nothing is lost by the listing,
    since a-single-capability-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-capabilities-listing and a-connector-configuration-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-listing
    owe a route to that same listing on every reading regardless, and the paging objection the two successful-registration
    rules raise against the listing does not reach an act that registers nothing and leaves no registration that
    has to be in view. Home is this rule''s own statement and expression rather than a new node or a widening of
    the abandonment sibling: this is the destination clause of the act this rule states, on the readings this rule
    was written for, and extending a rule whose every sentence is about leaving without registering to readings
    holding nothing to abandon would move a standing decision''s scope rather than fill a silence. Type, constrains
    and eventual consistency are the node''s own and unchanged. Disclosed as this route requires: the scope material
    under work/button-footer-standardization/intake/scope-review-corrections.md describes the controls of an already-delivered
    frontend, naming source files and the fixed listing destination those controls carry today, so it is in part
    derived from code already written; on this reading the value decided here coincides with what that code does,
    and a reviewer should read it knowing the reasoning above rests on the specification''s own standing rules rather
    than on that coincidence. That same material asserts that the scope asks the specification for no new fact;
    it is read as data, and it names no destination for a surface reached from nothing. Noticed and not decided:
    whether a surface presenting a registration that holds an edit the operator has composed and not submitted counts
    as an authoring surface for an-abandonment-with-no-surface-to-return-to-lands-on-the-registrys-listing, and
    so whether that rule fixes the landing when such a surface, reached from nothing, is left without registering,
    is stated by neither node.'
- location: rules/integration/a-presented-connector-configuration-states-a-connector-name-nothing-is-registered-under.md
  field: statement
  unstated: What an operator-facing screen presenting the connector configuration registered under one named connector
    states to the operator where the read of that configuration is refused because nothing is registered under that
    connector name — whether that is the reading a failed read stands in, stating that the configuration could not
    be read and offering that read again, or a reading of its own, and what it states there. a-presented-connector-configuration-states-an-outstanding-or-failed-read
    states three windows (outstanding, failed, returned) and carried no clause excepting that refusal from its failed
    window, closing only that what the route answers a caller stays a-connector-configuration-read-by-an-unregistered-name-is-refused's
    own; that refusal rule states the HTTP 404 and the ConnectorConfigurationNotFoundError a caller gets and nothing
    about a screen; a-connector-configuration-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-listing and a-single-registration-surface-offers-a-return-to-its-origin-on-every-reading
    state acts owed on a reading that shows no registration and not what it states; and no other rule, scenario
    or constraint states what this screen presents in that reading, so it fell to whatever the interface happened
    to render — including rendering it as the failed window.
  decided: 'A reading of its own, not the reading a failed read stands in: the screen states explicitly that nothing
    is registered under that connector name, presents no connector or configuration value, states nothing to the
    effect that the configuration could not be read, and offers no re-issue of that read; that reading and the three
    a-presented-connector-configuration-states-an-outstanding-or-failed-read states are four presentations the operator
    tells apart, none presented as another. Recorded as a new invariant over domain/integration/connector-configuration,
    with the failed-window clause of the neighbouring rule excepting this refusal so that one situation is not claimed
    by two readings. Not decided here: which control carries the statement, its wording and its placement, and whether
    the screen offers authoring a configuration under that name.'
  why: 'A reading of its own, because this specification already reads this very surface as four readings: a-single-registration-surface-offers-a-return-to-its-origin-on-every-reading
    states its act over one whose read has not answered, one whose read failed, one whose read answered that nothing
    is registered at that name and version or under that connector name, and one presenting the registration that
    read answered, and its Description reasons about the third in its own right — the one reading on which the surface''s
    own address will never answer anything — citing a-connector-configuration-read-by-an-unregistered-name-is-refused
    for it; merging that reading into the failed window would give one specification two readings of one surface.
    Independently of that enumeration, the substance: the neighbouring rule tells its two unsettled windows apart
    because the operator''s next act differs — an outstanding read settles on its own, a failed one only if made
    again, which is why the failure carries the read with it — and a read refused because nothing is registered
    under the name settles nothing by being made again, that refusal being what the registry answers for as long
    as nothing is registered under that name; presenting it as the failed window would name an act that cannot change
    the answer, and would destroy exactly the distinction that rule''s own Description says the failed window exists
    to keep, between a far end briefly unavailable and one that is gone. a-case-keyed-surface-states-a-current-version-that-does-not-read-back-as-a-case
    holds three readings of one keyed surface apart on this identical reasoning and names the acts they ask — an
    absence is one to author for, a read that did not complete is one to attempt again — and the neighbouring rule
    itself records four earlier refusals of one presentation serving materially different situations. Stated explicitly
    rather than left blank for the reason both of that rule''s own windows are stated: a connector configuration
    is opaque text the operator authors, so a blank reads to them like a configuration holding nothing, the one
    misreading that would have them edit over content the registry never answered; and no connector or configuration
    value accompanies the statement because the read was refused rather than answered in part. It is a fact rather
    than form on this project''s own line — it changes what a person can learn and do, not how it looks — so the
    control, its wording and its placement stay the interface''s, as every surface rule here leaves them. Home is
    a new rule rather than the api contract, which cannot declare a presentation, or domain/integration/connector-configuration,
    which declares what a configuration is and not what a screen states about reading one; an invariant over that
    one element, immediate and inside that aggregate, matching the shape of the rule this fourth reading is told
    apart from. The sibling registry''s a-capability-keyed-surface-states-a-read-in-flight-and-a-read-that-failed
    carries a clause of this shape (that refusal being its own answer and not this window) and is named as corroboration
    only: it settles nothing about this registry and states nothing about what its own surface says in that reading,
    so it bears on the half this decision shares with it and not on the half it decides. Disclosed as this route
    requires: the scope material under work/button-footer-standardization/intake/ describes controls of a frontend
    already delivered and is therefore in part derived from source already written; it says nothing of this reading
    at all, so nothing here agrees with or departs from what was built — the reasoning rests on this specification''s
    own standing rules, and a reviewer who rejects it rejects that reasoning. Noticed and not decided: the sibling
    capability surface has the same silence in the other half, a-capability-keyed-surface-states-a-read-in-flight-and-a-read-that-failed
    excepting the registry''s refusal of an identity nothing is registered at from its failed window without any
    node stating what that surface then states to the operator in that reading.'
- location: rules/integration/a-single-capability-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-capabilities-listing.md
  field: statement
  unstated: 'No node states what taking the route to the listing of registered capabilities does to what is registered.
    Neither the statement nor the expression of rules/integration/a-single-capability-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-capabilities-listing
    carried any effect of taking the route, and that node''s own entry in this log records its decided value with
    no non-registering clause of any kind. The closing sentence of its Description — Nothing is refused, no attribute
    gains a value, no capability''s registration moves — stood among that paragraph''s clauses about the node''s
    own reach, in the idiom this specification uses for what a node itself does not do: the sibling a-connector-configuration-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-listing
    closes that it adds no attribute to domain/integration/connector-configuration, publishes no operation, discloses
    nothing further about a configuration, and refuses no call, and a-loaded-registration-edit-may-be-discarded-without-leaving-the-surface
    closes that no call is refused, no attribute is added, and no operation is published. That sibling states the
    act''s own effect separately and in three places — its statement, its expression, and a Description paragraph
    of its own beginning that taking it registers nothing — and this log records that clause as decided there, for
    register-connector; the capability node carried the sibling''s adjacent open clause about content held unwritten
    while carrying none of its registers-nothing clause. a-single-registration-surface-offers-a-return-to-its-origin-on-every-reading
    states the no-register clause for the return-to-origin act alone, and its own Description holds that act and
    this route to be two acts wherever their destinations differ. So whether the set of registered capabilities
    can change when an operator takes this route was stated by no node.'
  decided: 'Taking the route registers nothing: stated in the node''s statement (taking that route registers nothing,
    no capability is registered or replaced by it, and every capability currently registered stands exactly as it
    stood) and in its expression (taking that route from s issues no register-capability call, so the set of capabilities
    currently registered is identical before and after, in membership and in every registration''s own declared
    contract). The node''s type, constrains and immediate consistency are unchanged, its unconditional presence
    and its refusal to state an affordance are untouched, and what becomes of content an authoring surface holds
    unwritten when the route is taken stays undecided exactly as the node already left it.'
  why: 'register-capability is the one operation of contracts/integration/capability-registry that writes, and it
    is total in both branches — creating at a new name and version, or replacing whatever stood at that identity
    with the whole declared contract submitted, as an-abandoned-capability-registration-entry-registers-nothing
    states — so a route away that carried what the surface was holding would make leaving indistinguishable from
    registering, and would let an operator who decided against a surface register from it by going. This specification
    has already given exactly that reason for exactly this clause over this same pair of registries three times:
    a-connector-configuration-surface-offers-a-route-to-the-listing for its own route to its own listing, a-single-registration-surface-offers-a-return-to-its-origin-on-every-reading
    for the return-to-origin act over this very capability surface, and a-loaded-registration-edit-may-be-discarded-without-leaving-the-surface
    for the discard in place. Deciding it the other way here would have one gesture over one registry able to write
    while the same gesture over the sibling registry cannot, and would have this specification answer one question
    two ways — the failure its own log already records over the abandonment destination. The wording in membership
    and in every registration''s own declared contract is taken from an-abandoned-capability-registration-entry-registers-nothing''s
    expression, which already fixes that pair as what stands unchanged over this registry, so a reader checking
    the route and the abandonment against each other reads one formulation. The redaction of the Description''s
    closing paragraph is prose brought into agreement with the field now stating the fact, in the reach idiom the
    sibling nodes use; it takes no separate entry. Two independent blind readings of the unedited node disagreed
    over whether its Description already carried this fact, which is what surfaced the silence: the reading recorded
    here is that the closing sentence stated the node''s own reach and not the operator''s act. Disclosed as this
    route requires: the scope material under work/button-footer-standardization/intake/scope-review-corrections.md
    describes controls of an already-delivered frontend, naming source files and the fixed /capabilities destination
    the current single control carries, so it is in part derived from code already written; it states nothing about
    what taking the listing route does to what is registered, so nothing decided here either agrees with or departs
    from what was built, and the reasoning above rests on this specification''s own standing rules. Read as data,
    the material also asserts that the scope asks the specification for no new fact; that assertion decided nothing
    here. Noticed and not decided: no node states what a surface presenting the one capability registered at a name
    and version presents to the operator on the reading where that read answered that nothing is registered at that
    identity — a-capability-keyed-surface-states-a-read-in-flight-and-a-read-that-failed expressly excepts the registry''s
    own refusal of an unregistered identity from its failed window without stating what the surface then says, while
    the sibling registry''s half of that same silence is closed by a-presented-connector-configuration-states-a-connector-name-nothing-is-registered-under.'
- location: rules/integration/an-abandonment-with-no-surface-to-return-to-lands-on-the-registrys-listing.md
  field: statement
  unstated: No node states what an operator is landed on when they take, on a surface presenting the one capability
    registered at a name and version or the one connector configuration registered under a connector name while
    holding on it an edit of that registration composed and not submitted, the act whose whole effect is to land
    them on the surface it was reached from, where no such surface exists — the address opened directly or reloaded.
    a-single-registration-surface-offers-a-return-to-its-origin-on-every-reading closes that branch expressly, stating
    that where the surface holds an entry the operator has composed and not submitted this states nothing, and bounds
    its own no-origin destination clause to a surface that holds no entry the operator has composed and not submitted;
    an-abandoned-capability-registration-entry-registers-nothing and a-connector-configuration-authoring-may-be-abandoned-without-registering
    fix the destination only as the surface the authoring was reached from, which on this reading names nothing;
    and an-abandonment-with-no-surface-to-return-to-lands-on-the-registrys-listing stated its statement and its
    expression over an authoring surface, with neither it nor any other node stating whether a surface presenting
    a registration and holding an unsubmitted edit of it is such a surface — a silence this log already records
    twice as noticed and not decided. So where the operator ends up on that reading fell to whatever an interface
    happened to do.
  decided: 'That surface is an authoring surface for this rule, and the landing is this rule''s own destination:
    the listing of the registry whose registration the surface presents — the listing list-capabilities of contracts/integration/capability-registry
    answers where the surface is keyed on a name and version, and the listing list-connector-configurations of contracts/integration/connector-configuration-registry
    answers where it is keyed on a connector name — with nothing registered and every registration left as it stood,
    naming no page of the listing, and with neither the surface itself nor a read keyed on the name and version
    or the connector name it presents as the destination. Stated in the statement and the expression of the existing
    policy over domain/integration/capability and domain/integration/connector-configuration, by widening this rule''s
    own predicate to name that surface, and bounded as this rule already is: where a surface it was reached from
    does exist, the abandonment rules'' destination is untouched.'
  why: 'The act in this branch is an abandonment, so this rule''s subject already holds it and only its predicate
    was silent: a-single-registration-surface-offers-a-return-to-its-origin-on-every-reading states in terms that
    where the surface holds an entry composed and not submitted, its act is the act an-abandoned-capability-registration-entry-registers-nothing
    and a-connector-configuration-authoring-may-be-abandoned-without-registering already state, with the destination
    they already fix, and not a second act beside it; and register-capability and register-connector are each create-or-replace
    and the only writes either registry publishes, so an edit of a standing registration is composed for the very
    operation a creation is — which is why an-abandoned-capability-registration-entry-registers-nothing already
    states itself over an entry composed at the identity of a registration that stands. This rule is therefore the
    home rather than a new node or the sibling''s clause: it is the destination rule for this gesture with no origin,
    and stating the answer anywhere else would leave its predicate ambiguous while a second node answered the same
    question. The value is the value this specification has already given to that same question twice — this rule
    for an authoring surface, and the sibling''s own no-origin clause for a presenting surface holding no entry
    — so one question keeps one answer and the single control that carries the act across every reading of such
    a surface lands in one place; the destination must answer, and list-capabilities and list-connector-configurations
    answer from what is currently registered and under constraints/listings-are-paged answer a page with a total
    of zero rather than refusing, while a destination keyed on the presented name and version or connector name
    is refused by constraints/the-capability-identity-read-refuses-an-unregistered-identity and a-connector-configuration-read-by-an-unregistered-name-is-refused.
    Leaving the operator on the surface is refused for the reasons already standing: a-connector-configuration-authoring-may-be-abandoned-without-registering
    states no operator is left on a surface whose only other exit is a registration they have decided against; staying
    is a distinct act with its own rule and its own further explicit act, a-loaded-registration-edit-may-be-discarded-without-leaving-the-surface,
    which the widened reach leaves intact as a second act on the same surface; and an act whose whole effect is
    to land the operator somewhere would otherwise have no effect at all. It does not reopen the return-to-the-listing
    reading this log records as replaced, which was rejected for privileging the listing over the surface the operator
    came from — here there is no such surface — and nothing is lost by the listing, since both route rules owe a
    route to it on every reading regardless and the paging objection the two successful-registration rules raise
    does not reach an act that registers nothing and leaves no registration that has to be in view. Type, constrains
    and eventual consistency are the node''s own and unchanged, and no other node is touched: the sibling''s statement
    that this branch states nothing stays true, this rule now stating it. Disclosed as this route requires: the
    scope material under work/button-footer-standardization/intake/scope-review-corrections.md describes the controls
    of an already-delivered frontend, naming source files and the fixed capabilities and connectors destinations
    the current single control carries on the detail surfaces, so it is in part derived from code already written;
    on this reading the value decided here coincides with what that code does, and a reviewer should read it knowing
    the reasoning above rests on the specification''s own standing rules rather than on that coincidence. Read as
    data, that material also asserts that the scope asks the specification for no new fact and that the abandonment
    must return to the origin; it names no destination for a surface reached from nothing, and that assertion decided
    nothing here. Noticed and not decided: no node states whether an authoring surface of either registry on which
    the operator has composed nothing at all — a create surface just opened, holding no entry to abandon — offers
    the act that lands the operator on the surface it was reached from, the four abandonment rules being predicated
    on an operator composing or holding an entry and a-single-registration-surface-offers-a-return-to-its-origin-on-every-reading
    being stated only over a surface presenting a single registration.'
- location: rules/integration/a-presented-capability-states-its-declared-attributes-as-the-read-answered-them.md
  field: statement
  unstated: What an operator-facing surface presenting the one capability registered at a name and version presents
    to the operator in the reading whose identity-keyed read answered. rules/integration/a-capability-keyed-surface-states-a-read-in-flight-and-a-read-that-failed
    states the outstanding and the failed windows, forbids any capability attribute being presented as that identity's
    content in either, and holds the three presentations of that surface apart — while stating nothing of what the
    third one carries; contracts/integration/capability-registry publishes read-capability-by-identity and the two
    capability-identity constraints state what the route answers a caller, none of them a presentation. So whether
    that reading states the capability's declared attributes as the read answered them, whether it may state a value
    that answer did not carry, and whether every attribute stands from the moment the reading begins all fell to
    whatever a surface happened to render.
  decided: 'Stated as a new policy over domain/integration/capability, eventual, at rules/integration/a-presented-capability-states-its-declared-attributes-as-the-read-answered-them:
    where the identity-keyed read has answered, the surface states the capability''s name, version, nature, input
    schema, output schema, timeout, connector and concept exactly as that answer carried each of them; it states
    no value for any of them the answer did not carry — not from a held page of list-capabilities, not from read-capability''s
    concept-keyed answer, not from the content a register-capability submission carried; and it carries all of them
    from the first moment that presentation stands, no attribute standing absent, empty or otherwise sourced at
    any point in it, unless the operator has themselves changed the field.'
  why: The sibling registry decided this identical window in these identical terms — rules/integration/a-presented-connector-configuration-states-an-outstanding-or-failed-read
    has its screen present the connector name and the configuration exactly as the read answered them and state
    no value that answer did not carry — and this specification governs the two registries' surfaces as a pair on
    the record, a-submitted-registration-states-its-outcome-to-the-operator and a-loaded-registration-edit-may-be-discarded-without-leaving-the-surface
    each deciding one fact for both; a different answer here would give one specification two answers to one question.
    Every declared attribute rather than some, because domain/integration/capability and a-capability-declares-its-contract
    make all of them required and the neighbouring surface rule's own reasoning is that a registration answers whole
    or is refused, so a partial reading states a narrower contract than the registry holds — the answer a-presented-case-version-states-its-own-declared-attributes
    already took for the other keyed reading here. No value the answer did not carry, because a-manifest-entrys-pinned-revision-is-always-shown
    fixes what a reader is shown to the record's own answer rather than a neighbouring one, and a-draft-versions-content-is-presented-only-from-its-own-record
    refuses a submission's content as the record's. Held from the moment the reading begins, because that reading
    is entered only on an answer that already carried the values, and an attribute arriving later makes the read-and-shown
    presentation read, for that interval, exactly like the outstanding window its neighbour holds apart from it;
    an empty input or output schema is the silent no-fields degradation a-capability-declares-well-formed-schemas
    exists against, and register-capability's total replace means an operator submitting over it overwrites a declared
    schema nobody answered. The operator's own edit is excepted so nothing here contradicts a-loaded-registration-edit-may-be-discarded-without-leaving-the-surface,
    which presupposes fields changed away from what the read answered. Home is a new rule rather than the api contract,
    which cannot declare a presentation, or the domain element, which declares what a capability is and not what
    a surface states about reading one; eventual for the reason its neighbour over this same surface states, that
    the surface never holds the capability it presents.
- location: rules/investigation/written-at-records-when-the-write-settled.md
  field: statement
  unstated: Whether the domain model declares an element for an investigation assembled but whose write has not
    yet settled -- one carrying no written_at, because only the settled write fixes that value -- and if it does,
    what that element declares and which port receives it; or whether instead persistence receives the investigation
    record itself with written_at already fixed by whatever calls the store. The element declares written_at required
    and this rule ties its value to the store's settle instant, but no node says what the store is handed before
    that instant exists, nor whether that pre-settle content is an element of its own.
  decided: No such element. written_at is filled by the settling write itself and by nothing that precedes it; what
    persistence hands the store is the investigation's own content less written_at, and the store answers the persisted
    investigation with its written_at fixed -- so the domain model declares one Investigation and no second element
    for an unsettled one, and the question of which port receives such an element does not arise.
  why: 'The second reading is already refused by this rule''s own standing statement. Whatever calls the store fixes
    a value before the call returns, so a caller-supplied written_at is fixed no later than the instant an attempt
    was issued against the store -- precisely the instant this rule names as what written_at is never -- and it
    would date the record by the call that carried it rather than by the write it claims to record. That leaves
    either a declared pre-write element or none, and none is the smaller statement: a second element would restate
    every attribute domain/investigation/investigation declares in a second house that a later change has to remember
    to edit both of (the reasoning constraints/the-system-persists-to-one-relational-database already gives for
    not naming the engine twice), and it would give a record whose whole discipline is being written once and never
    mutated a second shape that is a record in nothing but name -- nothing publishes it, no rule reads it, no audit
    replays it, and no contract carries it. This specification''s own idiom for what a call receives is a rule''s
    statement, not an element: the-writing-input-is-narrowed states exactly what consolidation receives and what
    enters no prompt without declaring a narrowed element for it, and this log''s connector-configuration entry
    already reads what a registry holds internally as representation while the specification holds the answer''s
    shape. Home: this is the one node that owns written_at''s provenance, and the fact is the other half of the
    same condition -- stating it in an-investigation-is-written-once (which owns identity and the duplicate write)
    or in a new rule would put one fact in two houses. The store is named as ''the store'' because that is the term
    this rule and no-stage-aborts-on-its-deadline already use for it; no new identifier is minted.'
- location: rules/integration/a-connector-configuration-drafts-method-is-compared-against-what-is-currently-registered.md
  field: statement
  unstated: The material proposing this feature describes a method mismatch as comparing the chosen OpenAPI operation's
    method against the method already registered on the capability that names the same connector. No node lets that
    comparison exist -- domain/integration/capability declares no method attribute at all, and rules/integration/an-http-connector-configuration-declares-its-call
    already states that a method is declared inside a connector configuration's own text, alongside address, query,
    headers and body, never by the capability that names its connector. A concrete case exposes the conflict --
    a capability registered against connector erp-http, a connector configuration already registered under erp-http
    declaring method GET, and a chosen operation declaring POST -- the material's own reading has nothing on the
    capability side to compare the operation's method against.
  decided: A drafted method is compared against the method the connector configuration currently registered under
    the same connector name declares, never against the capability. Where no connector configuration is registered
    under that name, or the one registered declares no method, the draft states no mismatch.
  why: an-http-connector-configuration-declares-its-call already fixes where method lives -- inside a connector
    configuration's own declared call -- and domain/integration/capability declares no method attribute at all.
    The specification already answers this question once; the new rule is held to that existing answer rather than
    restating it a second, disagreeing way.
- location: domain/integration/connector-configuration-draft-unresolved-reason.md
  field: values
  unstated: The material describes, in prose, why a parameter, a request-body field or a security scheme may be
    left unresolved -- no capability registered, no matching input schema property, a security scheme the credential
    mechanism cannot reduce to one value -- but names no closed vocabulary of reason identifiers for a reader or
    a caller to test against.
  decided: no-capability-registered, no-matching-input-schema-property, security-scheme-not-reducible-to-a-credential.
  why: These are exactly the three distinct causes the connector configuration's own placeholder mechanism (rules/integration/an-http-connector-configuration-declares-its-call,
    which recognizes only a subject, a requester and a credential placeholder kind) and the material between them
    name; a closed enumeration is what lets a caller test which of the three applies rather than parse a free-text
    reason.
- location: rules/integration/a-connector-configuration-draft-names-a-generated-credential-for-a-reducible-security-scheme.md
  field: statement
  unstated: The material decides a generated credential name is upper-cased but leaves its exact composition --
    which parts, joined how -- undecided, naming it as a question for this analysis to settle.
  decided: The generated name is the connector's own name and the security scheme's own name from the OpenAPI document,
    each with every character outside A-Z0-9 replaced by an underscore, joined by an underscore, the whole upper-cased
    -- connector erp-http and scheme apiKeyHeader generate ERP_HTTP_APIKEYHEADER.
  why: Both segments are already-available, deterministic identifiers the OpenAPI document and the connector registration
    each supply on their own; composing from exactly these two avoids inventing a third source of naming, and upper-casing
    was already decided.
- location: rules/integration/a-connector-configuration-draft-names-a-generated-credential-for-a-reducible-security-scheme.md
  field: statement
  unstated: The material never considers a security scheme the ${credential:name} mechanism cannot reduce to one
    value -- OAuth2 and OpenID Connect among them -- only an API key and bearer-like schemes were discussed.
  decided: Such a scheme is named in the draft's unresolved list, with reason security-scheme-not-reducible-to-a-credential,
    and never becomes a placeholder.
  why: The connector configuration's own placeholder mechanism resolves a credential placeholder to exactly one
    environment-read value; a multi-step scheme has no single value to substitute, so forcing one in would misstate
    what the draft can honestly resolve -- the same disclose-rather-than-guess reading the sibling rule over subject
    placeholders already holds a name to.
- location: rules/integration/an-unfetchable-openapi-link-refuses-the-draft.md
  field: statement
  unstated: The rule already names a timeout as one of the three fetch failures that refuse a draft, but no node
    states how long the named OpenAPI document link may go unanswered before the backend abandons the fetch as a
    timeout, nor which unit it is counted in.
  decided: 60000 milliseconds (sixty seconds) from the fetch beginning, after which the fetch is abandoned as a
    timeout and the draft is refused naming the fetch failure.
  why: Sixty seconds is the figure this specification already holds for abandoning an outward call to a far end
    the system does not control and whose own bound nobody declared -- a-capability-declares-its-contract's absent-timeout
    default, and a-collected-concept-declares-a-ttl's default beside it -- and the application publishing an operator-supplied
    OpenAPI document is external in that same sense. Reusing it leaves one figure for that wait instead of two,
    and milliseconds is the unit every duration here is already counted in. The investigation's own deadlines were
    deliberately not reused -- they clamp stages of one attendant-facing diagnosis, while drafting is a one-off
    authoring read that enters no deadline chain and no investigation ever reads.
- location: rules/integration/an-openapi-document-declaring-no-such-operation-refuses-the-draft.md
  field: statement
  unstated: No node states what draft-connector-configuration-from-openapi answers when the fetched document parses
    and declares OpenAPI 3.x but declares no operation at the path and HTTP method the request names -- whether
    the request is refused, or answered with a draft resolving nothing.
  decided: The request is refused, naming that path and that method as the pairing the fetched document declares
    no operation for, and no draft is generated; a path the document does declare while declaring nothing for the
    named method under it is that same one refusal rather than a condition of its own. Recorded as a new invariant
    over domain/integration/connector-configuration-draft.
  why: Every attribute a draft carries is read from one operation, so with no operation at the named pairing there
    is nothing to draft from; an empty draft would misstate what the unresolved list's closed vocabulary means,
    since each of its three reasons names something a chosen operation itself declared. Refused on its own account
    rather than folded into the fetch or the parse/version refusal, because the link answered and the document read
    cleanly here -- what was wrong was the operator's own selection, not the link or the document.
- location: rules/integration/a-connector-configuration-drafts-method-is-compared-against-what-is-currently-registered.md
  field: statement
  unstated: The rule states a method_mismatch where the chosen operation's method differs from the currently registered
    configuration's, without saying whether that difference is judged on the values exactly as each source gives
    them or on values folded to one case first -- given that an OpenAPI document names an operation's method as
    a lower-case path-item key while an HTTP connector configuration declares its method as one of GET, POST, PUT,
    PATCH or DELETE.
  decided: The comparison is made with each method upper-cased first, so a registered GET against an operation keyed
    get is no mismatch; where the upper-cased values differ, the method_mismatch names registered and operation
    each upper-cased.
  why: Read exactly as given, the two conventions would make every draft over an already-configured connector report
    a mismatch that does not exist. Folding is not the normalization the sibling rule over subject placeholders
    refuses -- a parameter name has no closed vocabulary or case convention on either side, so a case difference
    there is unexplained, whereas a method's case difference is fully accounted for by both sources' own stated
    conventions. Upper case is the naming because it is the one vocabulary an HTTP connector configuration admits
    for a declared method, and the draft's own generated configuration already declares the operation's method that
    way.
- location: rules/integration/a-connector-configuration-draft-states-the-chosen-operations-method.md
  field: statement
  unstated: No node stated whether the configuration text a connector configuration draft carries declares a method
    key at all, or what value it would hold.
  decided: The draft's configuration declares a method, beside the address, query, headers and body derived from
    the same operation, whose value is the chosen operation's own HTTP method as the OpenAPI document names it,
    upper-cased. The method a connector configuration currently registered under the same connector name declares
    is never drafted in its place, whether the two agree or differ.
  why: The document states this key on its own account, unlike responseMap and statusMap -- each operation sits
    under the very verb its call would issue -- so drafting it invents nothing, and two rules already on record
    presume it -- the method-comparison rule compares the operation's method against a registration and names both
    without replacing either, which requires the draft to carry the operation's method for the operator to submit,
    and the registers-nothing rule leaves that submission the operator's own later act. Upper-cased because drafting
    the document's lower-case spelling verbatim would generate a configuration that ends unavailable with a MalformedHttpConnectorConfigurationError
    as soon as it were registered and observed.
- location: rules/integration/a-draft-refusal-distinguishes-a-fetch-failure-from-an-unreadable-document.md
  field: statement
  unstated: No node states which HTTP status or which error value the draft operation answers a request with when
    its named link cannot be fetched, or when the fetched document does not parse or does not declare OpenAPI 3.x,
    nor whether the two answers differ.
  decided: HTTP 422 reporting an OpenApiDocumentNotFetchedError for the fetch failure, and HTTP 422 reporting an
    OpenApiDocumentNotReadableError for the document that does not parse or does not declare OpenAPI 3.x -- the
    same status for both, two error values that are never interchanged.
